knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Definite Integral of a Rational Function Using Partial Fractions

question.:question/worked-solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12 x + 12}{(x - 3)(x + 5)} &= \frac{12 x + 12}{(x - 3)(x + 5)}=\frac{A}{x - 3}+\frac{B}{x + 5}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
12 x + 12=A(x + 5)+B(x - 3)
$$

Plugging in $x=-5,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-48 &= -8B \\ B &= 6\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=3,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}48 &= 8A \\ A &= 6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{12 x + 12}{(x - 3)(x + 5)}=\frac{6}{x + 5} + \frac{6}{x - 3}
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }\frac{12 x + 12}{(x - 3)(x + 5)}\,\text{d}x &= \int (\frac{6}{x + 5} + \frac{6}{x - 3})\,\text{d}x \\ &= 6\ln|x - 3|+6\ln|x + 5|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6\ln|x - 3|+6\ln|x + 5|+C &= 1\ln|\left(x - 3\right)^{6} \left(x + 5\right)^{6}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{7}\frac{12 x + 12}{(x - 3)(x + 5)}\,\text{d}x &= [6\ln|x - 3|+6\ln|x + 5|]_{4}^{7} \\ &= (6 \ln{\left(4 \right)} + 6 \ln{\left(12 \right)})-(6 \ln{\left(9 \right)}) \\ &= \ln{\left(\frac{16777216}{729} \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3 x + 3}{(x)(x + 3)} &= \frac{3 x + 3}{(x)(x + 3)}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x + 3}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
3 x + 3=A(x + 3)+B(x)
$$

Plugging in $x=-3,$ we can eliminate $A$ and solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6 &= -3B \\ B &= 2\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3 &= 3A \\ A &= 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{3 x + 3}{(x)(x + 3)}=\frac{2}{x + 3} + \frac{1}{x}
$$

Now, we integrate, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }\frac{3 x + 3}{(x)(x + 3)}\,\text{d}x &= \int (\frac{2}{x + 3} + \frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ &= 1\ln|x|+2\ln|x + 3|+C\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}1\ln|x|+2\ln|x + 3|+C &= 1\ln|x \left(x + 3\right)^{2}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the definite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{3 x + 3}{(x)(x + 3)}\,\text{d}x &= [1\ln|x|+2\ln|x + 3|]_{-2}^{-1} \\ &= (2 \ln{\left(2 \right)})-(\ln{\left(2 \right)}) \\ &= \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$
